headline: Steady rain tonight brings first widespread Cascade snow; cool, showery weather lingers through Friday, then drier over the weekend.
summary: As of Tuesday afternoon, showers continue across western Washington ahead of an approaching front, with highs in the mid to upper 50s inland and low 50s along the water. Tonight the showers turn into steadier rain that lasts into Wednesday morning. Southwest winds pick up later this evening into Wednesday, peaking around 20 to 30 mph, mainly in the Southwest Interior through Shelton. The system brings the first widespread mountain snow of the season, and a Winter Weather Advisory covers all the Cascade zones from 5 PM Tuesday to 5 PM Wednesday. Snow levels start at 4000 to 4500 feet and fall to 3000 to 3500 feet by Wednesday morning. Forecasters expect about 4 to 8 inches at Stevens Pass, 1 to 3 inches at Snoqualmie Pass, and likely 6 to 12 inches in the southern Cascades, such as White Pass and Paradise. Travelers should check with WSDOT for road conditions. A pool of cold air high in the atmosphere (an upper-level low) then lingers over western Washington into late week, bringing spotty showers and cooler weather, with highs in the low to mid 50s on Wednesday and Thursday. Showers continue Friday, with light snow still possible in the Cascades. The system slowly moves out over the weekend, bringing drier weather into early next week. Overnight lows in the low to mid 30s have forecasters watching for possible frost or freezing conditions, but they have not settled whether that will happen and will keep monitoring it.
changes: The afternoon discussion described a front bringing steady rain tonight into Wednesday morning and gave specific Cascade snow totals by pass, while the morning one stressed showers and a slow-moving upper-level low. It also added a frost and freezing watch for the lows, and the advisory was extended to all Cascade zones.
